risks: El cluster carece de contenido más allá de un título: cualquier conclusión sobre el marco 'externo vs interno / datos vs no datos' sería inferencia desde el título, no evidencia.
Novelty=0.00 y corroboration=0.50 indican que la idea, si existe, no es nueva ni está corroborada por fuentes independientes.
Riesgo de sobreajustar el brief (docencia entry-level ya movida al perfil teaching) e importar conclusiones de un documento que no aborda esos temas.
Un único documento con engagement=0 no permite descartar que sea contenido promocional o de baja calidad.

critic.argument: The claim is barely a claim: it asserts only that a single document with a suggestive title proposes a two-axis taxonomy (external vs. internal LLM; data vs. non-data problems). The evidence base is a self-admitted single source with no ingested content — there is no methodology, no data, no corroboration beyond 0.50, and novelty is scored 0.0. What is being 'found' is itself a lexical artifact: the taxonomy is reconstructed from a title and subtitle, not from substantive text, so the 'finding' is indistinguishable from reading the heading. The two axes are generic distinctions already ambient in the LLM-adoption literature (on-prem/external deployment tradeoffs; data-centric vs. non-data tasks), so even if accurately paraphrased it is a decision framework, not an empirical result. It is also off-axis relative to the brief (technical leadership, coding agents, estimation, sequencing, productivity), meaning it supports nothing downstream. A single uncorroborated document with no content, framed as confirming its own title, is circular: the title is the evidence for the interpretation of the title. The stated confidence of 0.12 is, if anything, generous — there is no standing empirical finding here to be confident about.
